title: Yale Football Begins Its Ivy League Season
seoTitle: Yale Football Kicks Off Ivy League Season
subtitle: The team is a former national champion and returns to its peak under head coach Kevin Cahill
excerpt: The Yale Bulldogs take the field this weekend to open the Ivy League season after winning the national championship in 2025.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Yale Bulldogs kick off the Ivy League season this weekend after winning the national championship in 2025. Head coach Kevin Cahill, winner of the Eddie Robinson Award, returns to lead the team, which is already ranked 19th in national polls. The matchup against Holy Cross will be broadcast on ESPN+.

Yale Stands Out in the Ivy League

The team was already national champion in 2025, defeating Youngstown State and losing only to Montana State in the second round of the playoffs. In 2026, Yale remains strong, with expectations to maintain its dominance in the conference.

Coaching and Roster in Focus

Kevin Cahill returned from Lehigh and, despite losing running back Josh Pitsenberger, maintains a roster that looks to be the class of the conference. The head coach has a history of success, having been named the top coach at the FCS level.

First Game of the Season

Yale faces Holy Cross in Worcester, in a game starting at 2:00 PM (ET). Holy Cross brings a team that previously faced Yale in 2019, where Sean Kissel's defense stood out. The matchup will be crucial to gauge Yale's strength in the new season.

Broadcast and Coverage

All of this weekend's Ivy League games can be watched on ESPN+. The channel guarantees complete coverage of matchups between conference teams.

Outlook for the Season

With its recent track record and Cahill's leadership, Yale has a strong chance of repeating its 2025 success. The team has already shown the ability to overcome adversity, such as the loss of key players, and will look to solidify its position in the national rankings.

With information from Underdog Dynasty.
